name: Run
summary: Easy, steady running for aerobic fitness. Most runs should be in Zone 2, a pace at which you can still talk in full sentences.
setup: Warm up with 5 minutes of brisk walking or very easy jogging.
Decide the run's target: most runs are easy Zone 2 (about 60 to 70 percent of max heart rate). Accrue shows your zone live from Apple Watch.

steps.text: Land with your foot under your hips, not reaching out in front. A light landing on the mid-foot or a soft heel is fine; the key is where the foot lands, not which part touches first.
Let your knee and ankle bend a little as your weight comes over the foot. Hips stay level and tall.
Push the ground back behind you. The swing leg folds and comes through under the hip.
Arms swing forward and back from the shoulder, elbows near 90 degrees, hands loose. They do not cross the middle of your chest.

jointCues.cue: Run tall with a slight forward lean that comes from the ankles, not from bending at the waist.
jointCues.why: Bending at the waist pushes the landing out in front and loads the lower back.

jointCues.cue: Short, quick steps. Many runners do well near 165 to 180 steps per minute; raising your own cadence by 5 to 10 percent shortens the stride.
jointCues.why: A slightly higher step rate reduces braking forces and the load on the knee and hip.

jointCues.cue: Low and relaxed, not up by the ears. Shake them out every few minutes.
jointCues.why: Tense shoulders waste energy and stiffen the arm swing.

jointCues.cue: Elbows about 90 degrees, swinging back past your hip. Hands relaxed, as if holding a crisp without breaking it.
jointCues.why: The arms counter-balance the legs; a clean front-back swing keeps the trunk from twisting.

jointCues.cue: Slightly bent when the foot lands, in line with the second toe.
jointCues.why: A straight knee at landing passes the impact up the leg.

breathing: Breathe through both nose and mouth in a steady rhythm. On easy runs a 3:3 or 2:2 pattern (breathe in over two or three steps, out over the same) works for many people. If you cannot speak in full sentences, slow down to stay in Zone 2.
tempo: Easy runs: Zone 2. Accrue tracks pace, heart rate zones and VO2 max from Apple Watch.

mistakes.fault: Over-striding: heel lands far in front
mistakes.fix: Take shorter, quicker steps. Think of landing under your hips.
Keep about 80 percent of weekly running in Zone 2.
Swing the elbows straight back, like elbowing someone behind you.

safety: Increase weekly distance gradually, by about 10 percent at a time.

cues.text: Foot lands under the hips, not out in front
Tall, with a slight lean from the ankles
Elbows near 90 degrees, swing from the shoulder
